programme.title: The Secret Rules of Modern Living: Algorithms
programme.desc: Without people noticing, modern life has been taken over. Algorithms run everything, from search engines on the internet, to satnavs and credit-card security - they even help people travel the world, find love and save lives. Here, mathematician Marcus du Sautoy demystifies this hidden world by showing some of the most essential algorithms. He reveals where these 2,000-year-old problem-solvers came from, showing how they work, what they have achieved and how they are now so advanced they can even program themselves

programme.title: The Flying Gardener
programme.desc: Chris Beardshaw takes to the air in his helicopter and heads for Cornwall to create a tropical paradise in a school's backyard, regardless of weather and soil conditions. Along the way he takes a dip in the ocean in search of plants washed in from South America, and visits Britain's very own Jurassic Park

programme.title: Archaeology: A Secret History
programme.desc: Richard Miles concludes his series charting the history of archaeological breakthroughs by discovering more about the ancient common man. The investigation takes the archaeologist from the elaborate grave of Egyptian boy king Tutankhamun to the Danish resting place of the Tollund Man, who died as part of an Iron Age sacrifice more than 2,000 years ago

programme.title: The Search for the Lost Manuscript: Julian of Norwich
programme.desc: Historian Janina Ramirez tells the story of the first book written in English by a woman, Revelations of Divine Love by Julian of Norwich. The book was written in 1373 and presents an alternative viewpoint on man's relationship with God, which led to it being suppressed for more than 500 years. She travels from Norwich to Cambrai in Northern France, revealing how the book survived and the stories of women who championed it, and consults with academics and theologians about the book's importance

programme.title: The Architecture the Railways Built
programme.desc: Tim Dunn takes a trip to Swindon's railway village, which became home to Great Western's enormous works and he also explores the dark and secret past of Milan's station

programme.title: The Flying Gardener
programme.desc: Chris Beardshaw flies to the south west in search of hedges. He visits the gardens of RHS Rosemoor in Devon and Antony House in Cornwall. First broadcast 25 September 2006

programme.title: To the Manor Born
programme.desc: Audrey takes a holiday, but frets about leaving her beloved Grantleigh Manor in DeVere's hands. Penelope Keith stars

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth continues her search for a small country retreat - but her idea of small is not quite the same as everybody else's. Comedy, starring Patricia Routledge and Clive Swift

programme.title: The Fall and Rise of Reginald Perrin
programme.desc: First episode of the classic 1970s comedy, starring Leonard Rossiter as a middle-aged executive stuck in a rut and eager to learn the real meaning of life. When Reginald Perrin set out for work on Tuesday morning, he had no intention of calling his mother-in-law a hippopotamus. But he did, and from then on everything began to change. Originally broadcast in 1976

programme.title: The Fall and Rise of Reginald Perrin
programme.desc: Reggie takes his family to a safari park and finds the atmosphere in the car so oppressive that he steps outside to take his chances with the lions. Classic comedy, starring Leonard Rossiter

programme.title: Timewatch
programme.desc: Geologist Simon Haslett and tsunami expert Ted Bryant reveal the devastation caused to Britain when a 12m-high wall of water hit an area near Bristol in 1607 and claimed 2,000 lives. It crashed ashore with such ferocity that the geography of the coastline was altered for ever, yet despite being chronicled by eyewitnesses, the country's worst natural disaster has been forgotten with time

programme.title: Japan's Master of Restoration
programme.desc: Following Koji Mayuyama, an antique restorer known as The God Hand, who is the go-to man for museums and collectors all over Japan. A museum in Osaka asks the Mayuyamas for help with artefacts currently hidden away in their archive. An 800-year-old celadon vase from China and a 16th-century Totoya Chawan tea bowl both require their expert attention to be brought back to life

programme.title: The Joy of AI
programme.desc: Jim Al-Khalili looks at how man has created machines that can simulate, augment, and even outperform the human mind - and why this shouldn't cause alarm. He reveals the story of the pursuit of AI, the emergence of machine learning and the recent breakthroughs brought about by artificial neural networks. He shows how AI is not only changing the world, but also challenging man's very ideas of intelligence and consciousness. Along the way, the programme investigates spam filters, meets a cutting-edge chatbot, looks at why a few altered pixels makes a computer think it's looking at a trombone rather than a dog

programme.title: Lost Home Movies of Nazi Germany
programme.desc: Part one of two. Thousands of German attics have become dumping grounds for countless hours of private home movies, left gathering dust for decades and now giving an insight into the innermost recesses of life in Nazi Germany. This programme delves into these private collections, which are only now emerging, to reveal how Germans recorded the regime, featuring films from ordinary citizens as well as Nazi Party organisers, firemen, local officials and soldiers on the frontline

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Building of Britain
programme.desc: Turning his attentions to timber structures from the Middle Ages the former steeplejack visits England's oldest fortified building with a moat, Stokesay Castle. He also journeys to Harvington Hall near Kidderminster, Worcestershire, to see how bricks became an important part of timber-framed houses

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Archaeologist Ben Robinson unearths the ancient past of Greyabbey, a small village on Northern Ireland's beautiful Strangford Lough. This is a story of life from the sea - of the money-making kelp industry, and ingenious methods of catching fish

programme.title: Operation Grand Canyon with Dan Snow
programme.desc: Part one of two. The broadcaster joins a team of historians and geologists to recreate a pioneering 280-mile journey through the natural wonder that was led by explorer John Wesley Powell in 1869. Following in Powell's footsteps in the stunning yet challenging north Arizona landscape, Snow and the crew take on the area's rapids in antique wooden boats as they learn about the region's geological and Native American past

programme.title: Spencer Banks Remembers - Penda's Fen
programme.desc: Actor Spencer Banks reflects on his leading role in the 1974 Play for Today, Penda's Fen - a coming of age story written by David Rudkin and directed by Alan Clarke. Spencer discusses the challenges of taking on such a leading role and how this story of identity, sexuality and the notion of Englishness has steadily become a cult classic

Western, directed by and starring Kirk Douglas. With Bruce Dern and Bo Hopkins

Crime drama, starring Shia LaBeouf, Tom Hardy, Jason Clarke, Gary Oldman and Guy Pearce

Action thriller, starring Ryan Kwanten, Mickey Rourke and Freida Pinto

programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E
programme.desc: Patients whose visions of the world are rocked by life-changing events, including 44-year-old Sergio, who is flown in by air ambulance after a cycling accident. programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E

programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E

programme.title: Grand Designs
programme.desc: Adam and Tassy take on an abandoned water tower - a concrete column stretching over 20 metres into the Northamptonshire sky - and turn it into a fun family home. Their radical design includes a concrete interior with curved walls, slides, secret rooms, a fireman's pole and - up in the tank itself - a swimming pool and a sky garden. The plan is to sell their terraced house and get a mortgage to raise £400,000 and do most of the conversion work themselves - even though they have two young children already and a third on the way. It's wildly ambitious and gets off to a slow start when a steel reinforced floor takes forever to excavate, and they have to build a sound wall to reduce the hum from a nearby electricity substation. As concrete pours, their walls start to leak and it looks like their water tower doesn't want to be lived in without a concrete-soaked battle of biblical proportions

programme.desc: Kevin McCloud follows the progress of ex-advertising man Geoff, who is selling his luxury villa in Spain and moving into a caravan while he project manages the construction of a dramatically cantilevered steel-framed house on the Essex coast, costing a total of £700,000. programme.title: The Toxic Avenger (2025)
programme.desc: Bob Garbinger is the money-oriented CEO of a factory that is pumping out dangerous chemicals into the close-knit community of St Roma's Villa. Residents are poisoned by toxins, including widowed janitor Winston Gooze, who works at the factory and learns he has an incurable brain condition. Whistleblower JJ shares devastating information about the factory's reckless disregard for public safety and Winston undergoes a physical transformation in response to exposure to toxic ooze. He takes on the form of a hideously deformed vigilante and wreaks havoc on Bob and his brother Fritz. Comedy horror, starring Peter Dinklage, Kevin Bacon and Taylour Paige

They must fight to defend the human race as their enemies the decepticons plot to use this machine to rebuild their own world and destroy the Earth. Sci-fi adventure sequel, with Shia LaBeouf, Josh Duhamel and Rosie Huntington-Whiteley

programme.title: Justice League (2017)
programme.desc: Fuelled by his restored faith in humanity and inspired by Superman's selfless act, Bruce Wayne enlists the help of newfound ally Diana Prince to face an even greater enemy. Together, Batman and Wonder Woman work quickly to find and recruit a team of meta-humans to stand against supervillain Steppenwolf, but despite the help of Aquaman, Cyborg and The Flash, it may already be too late to save the planet. Sci-fi adventure, starring Ben Affleck, Gal Gadot and Henry Cavill

Comic-book adventure sequel, with Tobey Maguire, Kirsten Dunst, Alfred Molina, James Franco and Rosemary Harris

Superhero sequel, with Tobey Maguire, Kirsten Dunst and James Franco

programme.desc: The chef embarks on a culinary journey by sea and land to explore the Far East's most diverse food cultures. programme.desc: Off the coast of Yorkshire Siwrengale is heading out for the beginning of the North Sea whelk season. Skipper Darren Warters is on the hunt with sons Regan and Lewis. Reliance III is south east of Shetland, where skipper John Clarke is hunting for whiting, while Endeavour 5 is far off in the North Atlantic in search of squid - but when the prey proves elusive, the pressure starts to mount

programme.title: Trawlermen: Hunting the Catch
programme.desc: The crew of the scalloper Golden Promise pushes Force 6 winds to reach newly opening scallops beds ahead of their rivals. With the boat first to the grounds, they are in for a big pay day - but only once they cover the £8,000 fuel expenses to get here. Family owned trawler Adenia hunts for 1,000 tons of mackerel to sell to the lucrative Asian sushi market, and skipper Ivan Toms and son Rhys fish Cornwall's inshore waters in Maxine's Pride, one of the oldest trawlers in UK waters. Can they catch enough to give themselves a wage and put money aside for repairs?
